block-guide:
CORE/SEPARATOR A horizontal line (<hr>) between parts of the content.
MARKUP (checked in the editor) <!-- wp:separator --> <hr class="wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity"/> <!-- /wp:separator -->
<!-- wp:separator {"className":"is-style-wide","backgroundColor":"accent-3"} --> <hr class="wp-block-separator has-text-color has-accent-3-color has-alpha-channel-opacity has-accent-3-background-color has-background is-style-wide"/> <!-- /wp:separator --> A separator has HTML: write the <hr> even when the comment has no attributes; never <!-- wp:separator /-->. The class has-alpha-channel-opacity is always there (the default "opacity" attribute).
COLOUR The line colour is backgroundColor (not textColor): backgroundColor:"S" writes has-text-color has-S-color has-alpha-channel-opacity has-S-background-color has-background. A custom colour: style.color.background "#hex" -> has-text-color has-alpha-channel-opacity has-background and style="background-color:#hex;color:#hex".
OPTIONS Style variations: is-style-wide (a long line), is-style-dots (three dots instead of a line); in the comment's className and at the end of the class list. Without a variation the line length depends on the theme. align: "center" | "wide" | "full" -> aligncenter / alignwide / alignfull, right after wp-block-separator. Margin: style.spacing.margin top and bottom only. tagName "div" writes a <div> instead of the <hr>.
CHECK Reopen the editor (no invalid notice); the line shows on the front in the expected colour.
